items.abstract: <jats:p>In formation control, a robot (or an agent) learns to align itself in a particular spatial alignment. However, in a few scenarios, it is also vital to learn temporal alignment along with spatial alignment. An effective control system encompasses flexibility, precision, and timeliness. Existing reinforcement learning algorithms excel at learning to select an action given a state. However, executing an optimal action at an appropriate time remains challenging. Building a reinforcement learning agent which can learn an optimal time to act along with an optimal action can address this challenge. Neural networks in which timing relies on dynamic changes in the activity of population neurons have been shown to be a more effective representation of time. In this work, we trained a reinforcement learning agent to create its representation of time using a neural network with a population of recurrently connected nonlinear firing rate neurons. Trained using a reward-based recursive least square algorithm, the agent learned to produce a neural trajectory that peaks at the “time-to-act”; thus, it learns “when” to act. A few control system applications also require the agent to temporally scale its action. We trained the agent so that it could temporally scale its action for different speed inputs. Furthermore, given one state, the agent could learn to plan multiple future actions, that is, multiple times to act without needing to observe a new state.</jats:p>
title: Time and Action Co-Training in Reinforcement Learning Agents

items.abstract: <jats:p>Nonlinear stochastic systems pose significant challenges for model predictive control (MPC): nominal single-trajectory predictions may lack robustness, whereas long-horizon stochastic MPC with branching scenarios can become computationally prohibitive. Short prediction horizons reduce this burden but introduce myopia by truncating future system evolution. This work proposes radial basis function network reinforcement learning-based MPC (RBF--RL--MPC), which compensates for this truncation using a learned terminal-value function while preserving the constrained MPC structure. The terminal critic combines a quadratic-mean function with a finite Gaussian RBF expansion whose weights are fitted by closed-form ridge regression. Centers are initialized by k-means and expanded greedily, subject to a prescribed budget, when new samples are insufficiently represented. To stabilize the optimistic approximate policy-iteration process, the method further employs a growing experience replay buffer, frozen scaling and length-scale parameters after initialization, and parameter-space Polyak soft updates. Compared with deep neural network critics, the finite RBF representation provides a smoother and more controlled value surface, while avoiding the data-dependent growth in online computational cost associated with Gaussian process regression and k-nearest-neighbors approaches. Evaluations on a stochastic nonlinear benchmark and a Van de Vusse continuous stirred-tank reactor demonstrate reductions in closed-loop sum of squared errors of 75.22% and 94.80%, respectively, relative to baseline MPC.</jats:p>
title: RBF--RL--MPC: Finite Localized Value Functions for Reinforcement Learning-Based Model Predictive Control

project-title.title: Non-invasive monitoring of perinatal health through multiparametric  digital representation of clinically relevant functions for improving clinical intervention in neonatal units (Digi-NewB)

project-description.description: Using the clinical and signal data (cardiac and respiratory traces, video quantification of movement and sound) from a large cohort of hospitalised newborn and pregnant women recordings Digi-NewB aims to propose a new decision support system (DSS). This DSS will assist the clinician in his decision-making through non-invasive monitoring of sepsis risk and of cardio-respiratory and neurobehavioral maturations. The objective is to reduce mortality, morbidity and health costs for the hospitalised newborns. More precisely the proposal consist in: i) implementing a large targeted prospective multicentre neonatal cohort, recruited in six university hospitals, ii) identifying the most relevant composite indices to be included in the DSS iii) validating DSS acceptability and usability in the clinical management of the identified complex situations. To achieve these goals, a consortium has been constituted, under the coordination of a paediatric clinical network (GCS HUGO-France), with two SME (Voxygen-France and Syncrophi-Ireland) and four university groups with multidisciplinary expertise: in signal processing (INESC-Portugal and LTSI-UR1 France), in multivariate analyses (TUT-Finland) and in user centred design approach (NUIG-Ireland). The proposed new class of monitoring will lead to development of novel preventive and therapeutic strategies to counteract late diagnosis of sepsis and inappropriate evaluation of maturity. This will result in i) a decrease in sepsis related death and morbidity through early and personalized prescription of antibiotics, ii) a decrease in the risks of severe cardio-respiratory events and inadequate prolongation of hospitalization iii) a decrease in health costs. At the end of the Digi-NewB program the opportunity to productise the results will be evaluated. It would be a strong 'next generation' product which would secure a good market position. Feasibly development work will be carried out by the SME industrial partners.
